paraphrase: The ten avatāras of Viṣṇu are described (Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Paraśurāma, Rāma, and the rest), followed by the power of the chaste wife (Anasūyā's story).
speaker: Hari
notes: Chapter title ('daśāvatāra') and the Anasūyā story checked; the chapter's exact list of ten not read - low confidence.

checks.note: Partly confirmed. The chapter's colophon is 'daśāvatāra' (in 1.143.1), but its content differs from the paraphrase: it names Matsya (slaying Hayagrīva), Kūrma, Dhanvantari, Mohinī (Hari in a woman's form), Varāha, Narasiṃha, Paraśurāma and Rāma with his three brothers - no Vāmana, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha or Kalki - and then tells the pativratā story of the leper Kauśika's wife who stopped the sunrise (resolved by Anasūyā, 1.142.19-28), ending with Sītā. paraphrase: Immediately after death the embodied being takes an airy (vāyavīya) body, as a leech moves to the next blade of grass only when its front is firmly placed; the deluded do not see it leaving, staying or enjoying, but those with the eye of knowledge do; this airy body is called the conveyance-body (ātivāhika); when the ten piṇḍas are offered by sons, the piṇḍa-born body and the airy body become one.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: verse number checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the Garuḍa Purāṇa (Venkateshwara ed.; Pretakalpa cited as 2.chapter.verse) The leech image parallels Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.3 (U03).

paraphrase: The openings through which the life leaves the body indicate the destination: departure through the upper openings points to a higher course, through the lower ones to a lower course.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Only dharma follows the dead: wealth stays in the house, relatives at the cremation ground, the body on the pyre; the deeds, good and bad, alone go with the self.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: When death arrives, by the power of time some illness arises; the senses fail and strength goes; the pain is like the sting of countless scorpions; consciousness fades into insensibility; the breaths are moved by Yama's attendants standing near; with the breath in the throat the face froths; then the thumb-sized person (aṅguṣṭha-mātra puruṣa), crying 'alas', is taken from the body by Yama's messengers, looking back at his home; the truthful and faithful die easily, liars and betrayers in delusion; the messengers are terrifying, foul-smelling, with staffs and hammers in hand.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: Bhīṣma tells Yudhiṣṭhira how beings become pretas - through wrongdoing and the lack of rites - how they suffer hunger and thirst and afflict their kin, and how they are released (through gifts, śrāddha and hearing sacred texts); with the tale of five pretas.
speaker: Bhīṣma

paraphrase: On the road flows the Vaitaraṇī, a hundred yojanas wide, full of pus and blood; boatmen there say: if you gave the Vaitaraṇī cow, board this boat and cross in ease; one who gave the cow crosses easily, the one who did not is dragged through by the hand and pecked by birds; the gift of the Vaitaraṇī at the end of life is beneficial for men and burns away sin.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The ten piṇḍas offered by the sons over the first days are each divided into four parts: two parts make the preta's body, the third feeds Yama's attendants, the fourth nourishes the preta; the body is completed in nine days - the first piṇḍa makes the head, the second ears, eyes and nose, the third neck, shoulders, arms and chest, the fourth navel, genitals and anus, the fifth knees, shanks and feet, the sixth all vital points, the seventh the channels, the eighth teeth and hair, the ninth vigour, and the tenth completeness, satiety and the reversal of hunger.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The road of Yama: dragged by Yama's men with nooses, the preta travels about two hundred yojanas a day over thorns, stones, fire and burning sun, feeling pain when his body is burned; on the way lie sixteen cities - Yāmya, Sauripura, Nagendrabhavana, Gandharva, Śailāgama, Krauñca, Krūrapura, Vicitrabhavana, Bahvāpada, Duḥkhada, Nānākrandapura, Sutaptabhavana, Raudra, Payovarṣaṇa, Śītāḍhya and Bahubhīti - in each of which he eats the monthly piṇḍa given by his kin and laments the good he did not do; after a year he reaches Yama's city, with thirteen doorkeepers called Śravaṇas; sinners see Yama terrible, the virtuous see him gentle, crowned and radiant.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

paraphrase: The Brahmakāṇḍa grades the Purāṇas: sāttvika - the Viṣṇu, Bhāgavata and Garuḍa (highest), the Vāyu (middle), the Matsya and Kūrma (lowest sāttvika); rājasa - the Skanda, Padma, Vāmana, Varāha, Agni and Bhaviṣya; tāmasa - the Brahmāṇḍa, Liṅga, Brahmavaivarta, Mārkaṇḍeya, Brāhma and Āditya; the rājasa and tāmasa ones are not to be heard by seekers of liberation except for their sāttvika portions.
speaker: the Sūta (Brahmakāṇḍa)
